msg.content: 1 2 3 # Application Framework 4 5 All-in-one PHP framework and UI layer for building web and intranet 6 applications. 7 8 ## Introduction 9 10 The framework is designed to be a solid foundation for custom-built web 11 applications. The integrated functionality helps to focus on the application 12 logic, while being able to create the necessary administration screens, 13 APIs and more with minimal effort. 14 15 Note that it is not a CMS: it is exclusively a tool for building custom 16 applications. Supporting features are available out of the box, like the 17 notepad or image library, but anything your application needs to do must 18 be implemented by you. 19 20 One of the core functionalities of the framework is to provide an extensive 21 ecology of classes for accessing custom data stored in the database. 22 This includes complex filtering capabilities as well as a versioning 23 system with record state tracking (draft, published, etc.). 24 25 ## Features overview 26 27 - PHP helper classes for UI elements 28 - Form building system - every screen is a form 29 - Rule-based application environment detection 30 - Advanced database-stored data handling tools 31 - Class-based extensible templating system 32 - Localization system for UI translation 33 - News central (release notes, etc.) 34 - Event handling system 35 - Image media library and UI 36 - Tagging system and UI 37 - Versioning system with state tracking 38 - Disposables system for automated garbage collection 39 - API response caching (file-based, opt-in via Interface + Trait; TTL and manual strategies) 40 - SSO via CAS 41 - Interface Translations: English, German, French 42 - Build-time module documentation generators (Modules Overview, Keyword Glossary) 43 - Own ecology of supporting libraries 44 45 ## Requirements 46 47 - PHP 7.4 or higher (fully PHP 8 compatible) 48 - [Composer](https://getcomposer.org) 49 - MariaDB or MySQL database with InnoDB support 50 - Webserver 51 52 ## Installation 53 54 The framework can be installed as a regular Composer dependency. 55 However, the required application skeleton of folders and files 56 can currently only be generated dynamically using the 57 [Framework Manager][], which is currently still a private project. 58 59 Documentation on how to set up an application using the framework 60 is still in progress. In the meantime, the example application can 61 be used as a reference (see [Example application](#example-application)). 62 63 ## Example application 64 65 The framework includes a sample application which is used as a reference for 66 available features, best practices, and testing. It can also be used as 67 the basis for a new application. 68 69 You will find it in the `tests/application` folder. 70 71 **Installation** 72 73 1. Import the SQL file `tests/sql/testsuite.sql` into a database. 74 2. Open the folder `tests/application/config`. 75 3. Copy `test-db-config.dist.php` to `test-db-config.php`. 76 4. Copy `test-ui-config.dist.php` to `test-ui-config.php`. 77 5. Edit the settings in both files. 78 6. Access the `tests/application` folder via the webserver. 79 80 ## Composer commands 81 82 These are custom Composer commands that are available 83 when developing locally. 84 85 ### Build 86 87 The build step generates module documentation artefacts from `module-context.yaml` 88 files discovered throughout the codebase, updates the CTX `generated-at.txt` 89 timestamp, regenerates the API method index, and rebuilds offline event listeners. 90 91 ```bash 92 composer build 93 ``` 94 95 For the full development build (includes module glossary and keyword index): 96 97 ```bash 98 composer build-dev 99 ```

101	### Seed test database
   102	
   103	Populates the test database with the system users required by the test
   104	suite. Run this once after importing `tests/sql/testsuite.sql` (or
   105	whenever the system-user records are missing from the test DB).
   106	
   107	```bash
   108	composer seed-tests
   109	```
   110	
   111	The command requires the test database to be accessible and configured
   112	(see `tests/application/config/test-db-config.php`). On failure it
   113	prints a human-readable error message and exits with code 1, making it
   114	safe to use in CI pipelines.
   115	
   116	### Clear caches
   117	
   118	Clears all caches used by the framework, including the dynamic
   119	class cache.
   120	
   121	```bash
   122	composer clear-caches
   123	```
   124	
   125	## Developer Tools
   126	
   127	The `tools/` directory contains local-development CLI scripts. These are
   128	version-controlled and intended for developer use only — they are not part
   129	of the framework runtime.
   130	
   131	### CLI Utility Library
   132	
   133	`tools/include/cli-utilities.php` is the shared helper library included by
   134	every script in `tools/`. It provides four console I/O functions:
   135	
   136	| Function | Signature | Description |
   137	|---|---|---|
   138	| `writeln` | `writeln(string $text = '') : void` | Writes a line to STDOUT followed by a newline. Pass an empty string for a blank line. |
   139	| `color` | `color(string $text, string $color) : string` | Wraps text in ANSI colour codes. Supported values: `green`, `red`, `yellow`, `cyan`, `bold`. Returns plain text unchanged for unrecognised colour names. |
   140	| `prompt` | `prompt(string $label, string $default = '') : string` | Displays a labelled prompt and reads a trimmed line from STDIN. Returns `$default` when the user submits an empty line. |
   141	| `promptPassword` | `promptPassword(string $label, string $default = '') : string` | Like `prompt`, but suppresses character echo on Unix-like systems via `stty -echo`. On Windows or when `stty` is unavailable, input is read with echo visible and a warning is shown. |
   142	
   143	All functions are guarded with `function_exists()` so the file can be safely
   144	included more than once.
   145	
   146	## Build-Time Documentation Generators
   147	
   148	The `Application\Composer` namespace provides build-time utilities that generate
   149	two Markdown documentation artefacts automatically on every `composer build`:
   150	
   151	- **Modules Overview** (`docs/agents/project-manifest/modules-overview.md`) — a
   152	  Markdown table of all modules, their source paths, context doc locations, and
   153	  inter-module dependencies. Discovered from `module-context.yaml` files.
   154	- **Keyword Glossary** (`docs/agents/project-manifest/module-glossary.md`) — a
   155	  Markdown glossary mapping opaque domain terms to the modules that define them.
   156	  Application modules can contribute custom sections via the `DecorateGlossaryEvent`
   157	  offline event.
   158	
   159	To register a module for discovery, add a `module-context.yaml` next to its classes:
   160	
   161	```yaml
   162	moduleMetaData:
   163	  id: "my-module"
   164	  label: "My Module"
   165	  description: "What this module does."
   166	  keywords:
   167	    - "Widget (the core UI component)"
   168	```
   169	
   170	See [`src/classes/Application/Composer/README.md`](src/classes/Application/Composer/README.md)
   171	for full API documentation and the offline-event integration guide.
   172	
   173	## CTX Integration
   174	
   175	The project uses CTX to generate context files for AI-assisted development,
   176	and to provide an MCP server for integration with IDEs like PHPStorm to 
   177	access the framework's AI tools.
   178	
   179	### Related commands
   180	
   181	#### Start the MCP Server
   182	
   183	```bash
   184	ctx server
   185	```
   186	
   187	#### Generate all files
   188	
   189	```bash
   190	ctx generate 
   191	```
   192	
   193	#### Server information
   194	
   195	This fetches a JSON-lines list of configurations and tools available 
   196	in the server.
   197	
   198	```bash
   199	(echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test-client","version":"1.0.0"}}}'; \
   200	 echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}'; \
